merge_rule: An entry whose canon already exists in synonyms_q298.json and carries extends_q298=1 ADDS its abbr / syn / he forms to that entry instead of making a second one; every other entry is new. A form that Q298 already carries is a no-op, never a conflict, because both files resolve to the same targets.
doc: Q306: data/anatomy/synonyms_q306.json -- the ADDITIONS to Q298's synonym layer. A separate file rather than a rewrite of data/anatomy/synonyms_q298.json: the schema is the same, the provenance stays per round, and scripts/anatomy/q298/build_search_q298.py merges the two. Everything here was measured against the shipped pages first (docs/research/Q306_search_coverage_audit.md); no target is listed unless it resolves on at least one page, and anything that resolves nowhere is in `cited_but_not_shipped` with the reason instead.

entries.note: ADM is used for BOTH the hand and the foot muscle; the pages ship them as 'Abductor digiti minimi (hand)' and 'Abductor digiti minimi (foot)' and both are offered.
AP is also used clinically for 'anteroposterior' (a radiographic projection); here it resolves only to the muscle, because that is the structure the pages ship.
ED is used for extensor digitorum of the FOREARM; extensor digitorum longus / brevis of the leg and foot keep EDL / EDB.
Clinically LAD; Terminologia Anatomica calls it the anterior interventricular artery, which is the name the pages carry.

syn: medial collateral ligament of the elbow
entries.note: The pages ship an ulnar collateral ligament at the ELBOW and another at the WRIST; both are offered. The thumb UCL is not shipped separately.

The page name omits 'inferior'. MEASURED on the shipped geometry: this ligament sits at the ANKLE (z 73.8-100.3 mm in the Z-Anatomy frame) while the superior tibiofibular joint capsule sits at the KNEE (z 392.2-419.2 mm), so the shipped ligament is the inferior (syndesmotic) one.
As AITFL: measured at the ankle (z 83.5-103.9 mm), so the inferior (syndesmotic) ligament.

entries.canon: Medial collateral ligament of the ankle (deltoid ligament)
syn: medial collateral ligament of the ankle
entries.note: The deltoid ligament is a COMPLEX of four parts. The pages ship the tibiocalcaneal part as its own mesh and not the complex as one structure, so the search offers that part and says so.
Q298 already marks SIJ multi_part: the pages ship the three sacro-iliac LIGAMENTS, not a joint mesh. The spellings 'sacroiliac joint' and 'SI joint' are added here.
No page ships a mesh called a joint here; the search offers the talus, the calcaneus and the talocalcaneal ligaments, by the same rule data/anatomy/relations_q298.json states for joints.
As the subtalar joint: no joint mesh, so the bones and the ankle ligaments are offered.
The pages ship the metatarsophalangeal joint CAPSULES and ligaments as one mesh each, not a separate first MTP joint, so the search offers those and the great toe's own bones.

Shipped on the THREE FEMALE pages only. Q298 carried the singular 'Cooper's ligament'; the plural, which is how it is normally written, is added here. The OTHER Cooper eponym -- the pectineal ligament of the pelvis -- is not shipped and returns an explanation.
The Z pages ship 'Nail plate' (hand) and 'Nail plate (foot)'. The nail BED, the matrix and the digital pulp are not shipped and return an explanation (Q302).

MEASURED, and it corrects an out-of-date gap list: the nipple DOES ship, as 'Nipple (left)' and 'Nipple (right)' with the TA Latin 'Papilla mammaria', on the THREE FEMALE pages (Imaging F, Base F, Combined F). The three male pages ship no nipple and no areola -- they carry only 'Mammary region (skin)' and 'Inframammary region (skin)' -- so on a male page the search says so instead of returning nothing. Q302's gap 5 listed nipple and areola as absent; that is no longer true for the female pages.
As the nipple: shipped on the three FEMALE pages as 'Areola (left)' / 'Areola (right)' with the TA Latin 'Areola mammae'; absent on the three male pages.

cited_but_not_shipped.name: Psoas minor
cited_but_not_shipped.why: NO PAGE SHIPS IT, and no source this project holds contains it. Verified three ways: (1) all six pages' own structure lists contain no psoas minor -- only Iliopsoas / Iliopsoas tendon on the two Imaging pages and Psoas major / Iliacus / Iliopsoas fascia / Iliopsoas bursa on the four Z pages; (2) the pinned upstream Z-Anatomy catalogue (data/derived/zanatomy_inventory.json, commit 6c7f9016) has 3,572 named objects and none of them is a psoas minor; (3) the string does not occur anywhere in this repository. This is also the EXPECTED finding: the psoas minor is absent in a large share of people. Raja 2026 (Cureus 18(6):e111450, doi:10.7759/cureus.111450): "The psoas minor is a slender, inconstantly present vestigial muscle of the posterior abdominal wall. Classical texts report its presence in 40-50% of individuals" -- and in their own 30 cadavers it was found in 2 (6.67%; 3 of 60 sides, 5.00%), arising from the bodies of T12 and L1 and inserting by a long slender tendon into the pecten pubis and the iliopubic eminence (belly 4.57 +/- 0.46 cm, tendon 17.17 +/- 0.85 cm, total 21.73 +/- 0.45 cm). Patra 2024 (Folia Morphol 83(4):886-892, doi:10.5603/fm.99128) calls it "the most unstable muscle of the psoas group", found it in 12 of 30 cadavers, and notes that "the muscle's distal attachment to the iliac fascia may partially control the position and mechanical stability of the underlying iliopsoas". So its absence on these two bodies is a real anatomical possibility and not a segmentation failure -- but nothing here can prove it for THIS body either, because neither CT was read for it. Before Q306 the four Z pages answered this query with Psoas major at rank 1 and no note at all, which is a wrong answer rather than an honest absence.
